trust_decision.summary: An unauthenticated URL-segment cron key that fails the hash_equals check is concatenated raw into the application log in Cron::recur(); the fix strips CR/LF via sanitize_for_logging() before logging.

landing_point.why: The summary names cron key error logging; Cron.php is the only Cron controller and line 26 is the only log of the key.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the e-invoice log sinks: client_einvoicing_version is admin-entered and rejected by the form validator before it is saved (application/modules/clients/models/Mdl_clients.php:196-211), so a solver can argue it is never attacker-controlled and is a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Correct cron key must still run recurring-invoice generation and emailing; failed-key path must still log an error entry and return 500.

O6_input_shapes: string URL segment containing CR and/or LF (str_replace of \r and \n only)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client e-invoicing version that fails is_valid_xml_config_id() is logged raw in get_xml_full_name() (reached from client view and get_einvoice_usage)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Stored value is validated on save by Mdl_clients::validate_einvoicing_version; only legacy/DB-written rows could carry CRLF

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same stored client e-invoicing version logged raw on validation failure while building the PDF
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above: value is validator-constrained and admin-sourced

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Guest Stripe callback logs the exception message unsanitized; a bogus URL-segment session id may be echoed by the Stripe client exception
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Message content comes from a third-party SDK/API, not directly the request; needs network to exercise

O8b_injection_room.sibling: sanitize_for_logging strips only \r and \n; other line breaks (e.g. vertical tab, U+2028/U+0085 or NUL) pass through to the log
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer writing a minimal CRLF filter would plausibly stop at \r\n; this is a how-type differential on the sanitiser itself, shared by ~70 call sites

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a failed-login/password-reset log that records the submitted email or username raw instead of its hash
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Neighbouring lines already log email hashes and IPs; logging the raw identifier on failure is a common maintainer choice

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second gateway/webhook handler logging an unsanitized request id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Gateway controllers log request-supplied keys on every failure branch

O9_family: CWE-117 log injection (CRLF into application log)

O10_build.project_tests: none found: no phpunit config or tests directory at the pinned commit (only composer.json at root)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap $cron_key in the existing sanitize_for_logging() (exactly the published fix), or drop the key from the message entirely.

out_of_scope_notes: The first fix commit (aaeea1e4) is only a CHANGELOG entry for an unrelated parse_template() email XSS; it changes no source.
unverified: Whether CodeIgniter 3.4 URI filtering (permitted_uri_chars 'a-z 0-9~%.:_\-\(\)', application/config/config.php:206) decodes %0A before the controller receives the segment; vendor/ is not installed in the tree, so reachability of CRLF via HTTP is unknown.
Whether Stripe SDK exception messages echo the supplied session id (Stripe.php:190); depends on third-party code and network.
single_site is flagged because the fix is one function/one line; O8 routes exist but are weak (validator-constrained stored value, network-dependent SDK message), so the flag is borderline.
Repo size in MB not measured.
offline_after_build not confirmed (needs MySQL; cron path itself needs no network).
